serial_port.title: Warema WMS – Serial Port
serial_port.description:
The integration automatically searches for connected Warema WMS USB Sticks (FTDI FT232R devices).

Found devices:
{devices_list}

If your device is not listed or no devices were found, you can enter the path manually.

Examples:
- Linux: `/dev/ttyUSB0` or `/dev/serial/by-id/usb-FTDI_FT232R_USB_UART_…`
- Windows: `COM5`

data_description.serial_port: Path to the WMS USB Stick serial port (e.g. /dev/ttyUSB0 or COM5)

discovery.title: Warema WMS – Network Discovery
discovery.description:
Choose how to obtain the WMS network parameters (Channel, PAN ID, Network Key):

- **Enter manually** – You already know the parameters
- **Wandsender pairing** – Put the Wandsender (handheld transmitter) into pairing mode; the wizard captures the parameters automatically
- **Create new network** – Generate a fresh network and pair your motors to it

manual.title: Warema WMS – Manual Network Parameters
manual.description: Enter the WMS network parameters for your installation.

data_description.pan_id: WMS network PAN ID (4 hexadecimal characters, e.g. D70C)
data_description.network_key: WMS network encryption key (32 hexadecimal characters)

wandsender.title: Warema WMS – Wandsender Pairing
wandsender.description:
The stick is now listening for the Wandsender pairing signal.

**Action required:**
1. Open the battery case of the WMS Wandsender (handheld transmitter)
2. Press the **learn button** inside the battery case for approximately **5 seconds**
3. The LEDs turn green – the Wandsender is scanning for devices
4. When it finds the stick, the network parameters are captured automatically

**Status:** {status}

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Channel | {channel} |
| PAN ID | {pan_id} |
| Network Key | {network_key} |

Once the parameters are captured, click **Submit** to continue.

new_network.title: Warema WMS – Create New Network
new_network.description:
A new WMS network has been created with the following parameters:

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Channel | {channel} |
| PAN ID | {pan_id} |
| Network Key | {network_key} |

**Action required:**
Put your WMS motor(s) into pairing mode (consult the motor documentation – typically press the motor's pairing/learn button).

The motor will scan for a network, find the stick, and join automatically.

**Status:** {status}

Once a motor has joined, click **Submit** to continue.

**Step 1: Put Handsender into Pairing Mode**

1. Open the battery cover
2. Select channel with **(+)** button

init.title: Warema WMS – Options
init.description: Choose what you want to do.

menu_options.pair_device: Pair a Wandsender-bound device (e.g. slat-roof light)

pair_device.title: Warema WMS – Pair a Wandsender-Bound Device
pair_device.description:
Use this when a device does not show up under "Scan for new devices" even though it works fine from its handheld Wandsender (remote control) - for example the integrated lighting on a Lamaxa slat roof. Such devices are sometimes only ever paired to the Wandsender and never join the WMS network on their own, so the normal scan never sees them.

This captures the device's serial number by watching it announce itself while you operate it from the Wandsender. It does **not** change your network's PAN ID or key - only the new device is added.

device_settings.title: Warema WMS – Display: position direction
device_settings.description: Pick the cover whose Home Assistant display direction you want to change. This is a display-only setting and does not change the motor.

device_invert.title: Warema WMS – Position direction
device_invert.description:
Invert the open/closed direction for this cover in Home Assistant.

Use this for awnings (Markisen): by default a fully retracted awning reads as "open" because WMS reports it as position 0. Enabling inversion makes the retracted/home position read as "closed" and extending (shading) read as "open", with open/close commands matching.

This is a Home Assistant display setting only and does not touch the motor. To physically reverse the motor instead (also affects the handheld remote), use "Configure motor firmware parameters → motor rotation direction".

data_description.invert_position: When enabled: retracted = closed, extended = open.

select_devices.title: Warema WMS – Add Devices
select_devices.description: Found {device_count} new controllable blind(s) on the network that are not yet in Home Assistant. Select which ones to add.

configure_firmware.title: Warema WMS – Configure Motor Parameters
configure_firmware.description:
These are persistent on-device settings stored in the motor itself. They survive power cycles and also apply when you operate the motor via the handheld remote. Pick the device whose firmware parameters you want to read and change.

{device_count} configurable device(s) available.

data_description.copy_from: Optionally load the current parameters of another blind; defaults to the selected device's own values.

firmware_params.title:
Motor parameters
{device_name}
firmware_params.description: Only changed fields are written to the motor.

data_description.manual_position: Target position (0–100 %) when the manual down button on the handheld is pressed; 0 = fully open, 100 = fully closed.
data_description.manual_angle: Slat angle (0–75 °) set after reaching the manual position; 0 = horizontal, 75 = fully closed.
data_description.manual_dwell_time: Wait time (0–254) before the slats are tilted after manual positioning.

data_description.comfort_position: Target position (0–100 %) of the comfort scene recalled with the comfort button on the handheld.
data_description.comfort_angle: Slat angle (0–75 °) of the comfort scene; negative values tilt inward, positive outward.
data_description.comfort_auto_enabled: Enables or disables the sensor automatics, e.g. sun and wind automation on the handheld.

data_description.absent_position: Target position (0–100 %) when the Away status is active; typically 95 % for maximum protection.
data_description.absent_angle: Slat angle (0–75 °) when the Away status is active; typically 75 ° for fully closed.

data_description.run_time_up: Seconds (0–254) for a full travel from the bottom to the top end stop; must match the actual installation height.
data_description.run_time_down: Seconds (0–254) for a full downward travel; should be roughly equal to the run time up.
data_description.calibration_up: Extra motor run time in seconds (0–254) after reaching the top end stop for accurate referencing; typically 3 s.
data_description.calibration_down: Extra motor run time in seconds (0–254) after reaching the bottom end stop; typically 1 s.

data_description.tilting_time: Seconds (0–50.8, step 0.2 s) for a full 180° slat rotation from one end to the other; typically 1.6 s.
data_description.min_angle: Lowest allowed slat position in degrees (-127–+127); prevents over-tilting inward; typically -75 °.
data_description.max_angle: Highest allowed slat position in degrees (-127–+127); prevents over-tilting outward; typically +75 °.
data_description.tilting_steps: Number of intermediate steps (0–254) per full slat rotation; more steps give finer angle resolution; typically 10.

data_description.motor_rotation: Reverses the motor rotation direction; enable if the blind moves up on a Down command or vice versa. For a display-only reversal that does not change the motor, use Options → "Display: position direction (awnings)".

error.write_failed: Writing parameters to the motor failed. The motor may be unreachable, asleep, or in use. Wake it via the handheld remote and try again. Check the Home Assistant log for per-step details.
error.ref_unreachable: Could not read the values from the source blind; the selected device's own current values were loaded instead. The motor may be unreachable or asleep.

abort.not_loaded: The integration is not loaded. Make sure the WMS stick is connected and the integration is running, then try again.
abort.no_new_devices: No new devices were found on the network. Make sure the new blinds/motors have been added to the WMS network and have completed a reference run (full open/close cycle).
abort.no_configurable_devices: No devices in this integration support firmware parameter configuration. Only Actuator UP (type 20), Plug Receiver (type 21) and Actuator 230V UP (type 2E) are supported.
abort.cannot_read_params: Failed to read parameters from the motor. The device may be unreachable. Wake the motor (e.g. with the handheld remote) and try again.
abort.cannot_connect: Failed to communicate with the WMS USB Stick while pairing. Check the serial port and connection, then try again.
abort.pairing_timeout: No Wandsender/device completed pairing in time. Make sure the Wandsender is in learn mode and within range, then try again.
abort.device_not_in_scan: The device announced itself (its serial number was captured) but did not answer the follow-up network scan - it may have gone back to sleep. Check the Home Assistant log for its serial number, then try "Scan for new devices" once it is active again.
